chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Halabi, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a house that had not been partitioned, and some of its residents gave charity with their share of the house. He said, 'It is permissible.' I said, 'What if it was a gift?' He said, 'It is permissible.' He said, 'And I asked him about a man who housed another man in his house during his lifetime.' He said, 'It is permissible for him, and he does not have the right to evict him.' I said, 'For him and his descendants?' He said, 'It is permissible.' And I asked him about a man who housed another man in a house and did not specify any time for him. He said, 'The owner of the house may evict him whenever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for donating a share of an undivided house or granting housing rights in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of disposing of undivided shares (*musha*) through charity or gift, reflecting the Shia emphasis on individual ownership rights within joint property. It further distinguishes between temporary tenancy and permanent habitation rights, noting that without a specified term, the owner retains the right to evict, a principle crucial for understanding Islamic property law and inheritance dynamics.
